summary: 1. A 4-Sep 04:00 shift-handover meeting is the only new meeting note this pass. 2. It catches an operator bypassing the mandatory brake-check sign-off and driving straight into the pit — he denied it when first asked, then admitted it once confronted with direct observation; a formal warning is being issued. 3. The same meeting finds and fixes two drill safety gaps (no flashback arresters, an accumulator being recharged with nitrogen) the same night. 2. 4. The meeting runs its own live investigation into a ~204,000-ton production discrepancy — the third independent naming of a figure in the 200,000-205,000 ton range this KB has tracked in a week, after the 1-Sep director-review meeting's "200,000-205,000 ton" survey-vs-tally gap and the 3-Sep weekly HOD meeting's "~204,000 tons of survey variance." This is the first source to propose a mechanism: operators suspected of logging the final hour's trips 15-20 minutes early and attributing them to the wrong hourly window. 5. By the meeting's own math, combining the affected hours nets out close to a normal trip rate — arguing against this fully explaining a discrepancy of that size, a caveat logged alongside the finding rather than treated as resolved. 3. 6. The Day 10 survey workbook (260904-INX-SUM.xlsx) finally landed, and with it Day 9's data — which never got its own standalone file, appearing only as a row inside Day 10's own table. 7. Day 9 posts the cycle's deepest gap yet (-23.64%, trucks 21,080 / survey 17,049). 8. Day 10 reverses to the cycle's first positive gap (+7.77%, trucks 20,615 / survey 22,351). 9. MTD through Day 10: trucks 193,223 BCM vs survey 182,351 BCM, -5.96%. 4. A batch of seven historical broken-stock emails (26-Aug through 1-Sep) backfilled into RAW alongside the new Sep 4 copy, all sharing the same inline-image, no-plain-text pattern already flagged as OCR-unreliable at the 105th pass — confirming this is a standing sender-side formatting choice across at least eight consecutive emails, not an isolated bad scan. 5. Truck 347 stood roughly 45 minutes at the fuel bay awaiting the diesel tanker — logged as a fifth event in the refuelling-area pattern, alongside the meeting's first concrete process fix for the fueling-delay side of that pattern (fuel immediately after the 7:00-7:30 toolbox meeting instead of 8:00, two dedicated attendants). Sixteen already ingested at prior passes. One genuinely new: the 4-Sep shift-handover meeting, written verbatim to RAW. Important References folder re-checked: 39 files, no new or updated content since the 105th/106th passes' last check. Wiki compile: updated [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] (Day 9 retroactive data, Day 10's first positive gap, MTD figures, the shift-handover meeting's 204,000-ton figure and proposed tally-timing mechanism, broken-stock OCR limitation confirmed standing), [[safety-inspection-patterns]] (brake-check bypass, drill safety gaps), [[refuelling-area-safety-pattern]] (fifth event — Truck 347 — and the first concrete fueling-timing process fix), [[kaizen-load-haul-efficiency]] (per-operator KPI framework proposal, trip-timing tally investigation), [[overspill-material-management]] (Stage 6 opening still urgent, still under-resourced) — five articles' `Last updated` bumped to 2026-09-04 (107th pass). `Wiki/INDEX.md` one-line descriptions refreshed for all five.
